head.h1: Brunch at Home Dubai: A Hosting Guide
head.meta_description: Plan brunch at home in Dubai with menu ideas, service options, kitchen checks and clear pricing questions for a relaxed morning with guests.

opening_paragraph: Brunch at home in Dubai can be as relaxed or as polished as you wish: a generous sharing table, eggs cooked to order or a sequence of plated dishes. Start with the guest list, the time you would like to eat and the space available, then choose the menu and service around them.

new_paragraphs: Combine a few savoury dishes with fresh fruit, pastries and a considered sweet finish. Eggs, a vegetable dish and a substantial sharing plate give guests choice without overwhelming the kitchen. Offer water, tea, coffee and agreed juices throughout the meal.
Ask which dishes can be prepared in advance and which need cooking just before service. One live station can add interest, provided the kitchen has the space, power and ventilation to support it.

replace_in_block.block_on_your_page: Choose delivery or a chef at home
replace_in_block.new_heading: Choose delivery or a chef at home
new_paragraphs: Delivered platters work when you have someone to set out the food and manage the table. A chef at home is useful for hot dishes prepared to order; service staff can look after drinks, clearing and replenishment. Confirm exactly who is responsible for each task.

Bespoke chef-led plated dining is a different format from a delivered brunch or sharing menu. myCHEF’s AED 700–950 per-person plated range should not be treated as a universal brunch price. Ask for the format and inclusions you actually want.

Allow time for arrival, setup and the first drinks before inviting everyone to eat. An indoor alternative is useful for an outdoor table, and a shaded serving area helps keep the experience comfortable.
For families, confirm children’s portions and keep hot equipment outside busy walking routes. Collect dietary requirements early so alternatives can be planned with the full menu.

Compare the complete service, including the menu, guest count, preparation, staffing, equipment, delivery and clear-down. A per-person price is useful only when the inclusions are clear. Ask which elements are fixed and which can change if your plans change.

Share allergies and other dietary requirements before confirming. The culinary partner should explain the preparation arrangements and any remaining cross-contact risk. Review the payment schedule, cancellation terms and change deadlines in your written booking.

Send the date, Dubai address, expected guest count and preferred service time, together with your menu ideas and venue details. Photos of the kitchen or service area can help the team assess what is practical.

myCHEF typically replies within 15 minutes between 9am and 9pm Dubai time. The tailored proposal follows once the requirements and availability have been reviewed. A first reply is an acknowledgement, rather than confirmation that a chef or date has been secured.
